bearings.paper_claim: Pooled sector-FE models: (1) log Contrib on G(t-1), G(t), Neg(t-1), Midterm, Pres, Tossup, Trend; (2) RShare by chamber on growth, Shift, RMajNow, Midterm, Pres; (3) log Lobby on lagged log Lobby, growth, Neg, Unified. Growth z-scored within sector; CPI-deflated dollars; wild cluster bootstrap by sector; proposed sample 2008-2025 with 5 initial sectors (expansion to about 70 BEA industries allowed).
bearings.system_side: sgs_registry.R builds C1-C3 and L1-L3 as sector-FE tests with wild cluster restricted bootstrap by sector (Webb six-point weights); sgs_estimate.R header confirms this inference. Growth z-scoring and log DVs not checked in code here (the registry default DV is levels; see next bearing).
bearings.transfer_conditions: Holds only as a statement of the memo design. The build departs from it (next bearing), so build results must not be read as memo tests.
bearings.verifier_note: Equations 1-3, z-scoring, CPI deflation, wild cluster bootstrap and 2008-2025 window confirmed in text Sections 4.1-4.3, 5 and 6.1. Memo model 2 also includes Midterm and Pres, which the rel omits. Code lines confirmed: C and L loops at registry 112-120; WCR with Webb six-point weights at estimate.R 1-10.

bearings.paper_claim: Both growth timings belong in one regression (distributed lag) because separate models would each pick up part of the other effect. Totals get Tossup = 1 - abs(2P - 1), not a signed Republican-gains term. A Neg dummy, a Trend and lagged log lobbying are included. Lobbying uses Unified control.
bearings.paper_location: Section 4.1 items 1, 7 and 8; Section 4.3; Section 5 equations 1 and 3
bearings.system_side: Registry runs C1, C2 and C3 as separate single-growth models, not jointly. Contribution controls are pres_year, midterm_year, exp_dem_house, exp_dem_senate; the core has no Tossup, Neg or Trend term. Lobbying adds cur_dem_house and cur_dem_senate and has no lagged DV. Contribution DV defaults to real dollar levels (contributions_real_m), with logs only in robustness. Primary window 2020-2025 (R8). The g_pos/g_neg asymmetry split is an EXTENSION family from the 2026-09-26 rulings, not the core spec, so the rel statement that decline years use it as the core is softened. The expected-control terms are not P in levels: per year they come from an IEM annual mean, a binary forecaster final call (Democrats at or above 218 House or 51 Senate seats), or a market snapshot. The 2023 value is a final call flagged as measured Nov 2024, after the year.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Applies to every CORE C and L result. Rulings R4-R8 and the 2026-09-26 rulings may supersede parts of the memo, but results from separate-timing, signed-control models should not be reported as tests of memo H1 or H3.
bearings.verifier_note: Memo text (Section 4.1 items 1, 7, 8; 4.3; equations 1 and 3) confirmed. Code confirms separate C1-C3, no core Neg, Trend, Tossup or lagged DV, and window 2020-2025. Softened: ASYM is an extension family, and exp_dem is a per-year method mix (including a 0/1 call measured after the year), not P levels as the rel summary says.

bearings.paper_claim: Probability of majority control is the preferred projected-control measure because access comes with majority status (Cox and Magar 1999, about 36,000 USD per member, cited and not verified here). Expected seat change is kept only as a robustness check. Q4 asks how quickly PAC giving tracks changing expectations within a cycle; Q7 asks about an event study around expected flips.
bearings.system_side: SEATS-W is a weekly test in report 221444: 17 weeks, 2022 House only (2020 and 2024 not usable yet). Dependent variable is the Democratic share of gross positive receipts. Regressor is the prior-week change in 538 Lite expected Democratic seats, with a week-of-cycle trend. House level, pooled-dollar (the first row of the primary table): -3.36 pp per seat, block-bootstrap p 0.11 and 0.10, not significant. The -3.47 pp figure with p 0.0086 and 0.0174 (Holm 0.034 and 0.070) is the equal-sector variant. Senate level is null in both weightings (equal-sector +6.23, p 0.65; pooled-dollar +3.99, p 0.81).

bearings.paper_claim: Election-cycle controls use Pres and Midterm dummies with odd years as the baseline. Industry forecasts (IBISWorld, trade outlooks) are used only to predict 2026 spending after estimation and are never mixed into the estimated growth variable.
bearings.paper_location: Section 4.2 (cycle controls); Section 4.1 item 6 (forecasts used only at prediction)
bearings.system_side: The cycle model projects with M = B exp(phi dP + d_h) (1 + x/2), where dP = Pres(c) minus Pres(c-2) is a presidential-cycle difference, not a Midterm dummy with odd-year baseline. The IBISWorld real growth path, lagged one year, enters only through the projection term x. Forecast growth is kept out of estimation in this model. The sector study does put predicted_growth_pct on the right-hand side in C3 and L3 (sgs_registry.R:30), which the memo prohibits; that departure is outside this bearing.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Supports only the forecast product split between estimation and projection. Does not cover the sector study C3 and L3 tests, and the presidential-difference term is not the memo Midterm and Pres dummy set.
bearings.verifier_note: Memo Section 4.1 item 6 and 4.2 confirmed. Code comment at giving_forecast.py 1391-1397 confirmed for the IBIS one-year lag and projection-only role. The Pres and Midterm dummy wording is not what the code uses, so the system side is corrected. Ruling R6 was not opened.

related.why: Imai and Kim (2021) on two-way fixed effects for causal inference supports caution about the memo year FE plan. The text has no lagged-dependent-variable discussion, so the rel attribution about a lagged DV with few units is not carried over.

Kim, Stuckatz and Wolters (2020) find interest-group donations directly tied to subsequent lobbying, supporting separate modeling of giving and lobbying. The unit is interest group, not firm as the rel says.
Finds minimal overlap between organizations that lobby and organizations making campaign expenditures. Bears on memo questions 2 and 8.
Partisan ties with the House majority party are valued by clients, and the paper tests firm value around the 2011 change in House control. Relevant to the access-with-majority logic in H2 and H4.
Estimates firm-level returns to lobbying (abstract and counterfactuals). Relevant to the deep-pockets reading; the link to H1 is interpretive.
Introduces the common-space CFscores that DIME uses for the RShare outcome.
Reports lobbying network dynamics with periodicity synchronized with the presidential election cycle, supporting the memo Pres and Midterm controls in the lobbying model.
Covers Fairshake and the concentrated crypto lobby, supporting the memo choice to analyze crypto separately.
Paul earlier report on five financial sectors using FEC, FDIC, SEC and LDA data. Overlapping sectors and sources, but a snapshot report, not the sector-year panel.

summary_issues: SEATS-W headline -3.47 pp (p 0.0086 and 0.0174) is the equal-sector variant. The pooled-dollar primary row is -3.36 pp with p 0.11 and 0.10 and is not significant. The rel does not say which weighting it reports.
SEATS-W regressor is the prior-week change in 538 Lite expected Democratic seats with a week-of-cycle trend, not the level of expected seats as the summary states.

The no-stable-shift figure (-0.04, p 0.76) is the SHIFT-Chamber-PV preview: 80 rows, 4 residual df, below the 6-year minimum. Core SHIFT-Chamber and SHIFT-House are NOT ESTIMABLE in report 221444 (5 of 6 years). The SATURATED at 2 years wording does not match that report.

Majority probability P is not what enters as exp_dem levels. The panel uses per-year IEM annual means, a binary forecaster final call (Democrats at or above 218 House or 51 Senate seats), or a market snapshot. The 2023 value is a final call measured Nov 2024, after the year, which departs from the memo measured-before-money rule (Section 4.3). The rel does not record this.
L3-LV year-FE coefficient -0.4765 (rel -0.477) is not significant (p 0.15, CI -1.02 to 0.73). The rel presents the sign flip without that qualifier.

The within-cycle signal claim is overstated: equal-sector House lag (-3.05, p 0.014) and 538 Classic equal-sector level (-3.59, p 0.036) are also negative. All rest on one cycle, as the report itself says.
